chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: Touring with Wilbur Sweatman and George Stevens's firing
summary: He retells joining Sweatman, touring New England, then going to New York where singer George Stevens was fired and the band quit.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you come into New York? Let's get into that.

I met Swetman. Wilbur Swetman, and Swetman was looking for a piano player, and I was out of a job -- well, I wasn't out of a job, but you know, it was coming on summer, and I just set three guys up there at Lake George, a summer place, so I said, "Yeah, I'll go" -- so then he ...
And then he used to play three clarinets at one time. And --
You came to New York with him?

Yeah, and first we toured New England and then we come to New York. When I first came to New York, George Stevens -- he was a singer, played banjo, and he got a job and asked me if I wanted to play with him, and I said, 'Yeah' so we went up there to New Rochelle right outside of New Rochelle there, and played there for about a week, and the man fired George.

Wait a minute. The man said, 'Where you going' -- and I said, 'Well, you fired the boss.' So he said so what, and I said, 'Well, when you fire the boss, you fire all of us' -- so he said, the guy was getting fresh with the girls, with the women, with the people - and he was a good looking boy, he could sing, too.
So he let you all stay on, huh?
No -- we all quit and come on back. That's when I starved here for 8 months around New York, and --
